text: Holding I R F C? Don't average down before you see this. Multibagger, or trap?
In January 2021, I R F C listed at twenty six rupees. By July 2024, it touched two hundred twenty nine. Almost nine times your money.
Today it's near eighty one. Sixty five percent below the top. So what does I R F C actually do?
It's the money arm of Indian Railways. It borrows from the market, pays for trains, coaches, wagons and railway projects, and leases them to the Railways for thirty years.
The Railways pay back the cost, plus a small fixed margin. So no bad loans. Its book is now about four point eight lakh crore rupees, and over ninety percent of it is the Railways.
Latest results. Revenue up twenty three percent. Profit up ten percent, to one thousand nine hundred fifty eight crore. Plus a dividend of one rupee fifteen paise.
But here's the catch. Interest costs jumped thirty percent, faster than revenue. And the government keeps selling its shares. Both sales this year pushed the price down.
So, multibagger or trap? Neither, for now. At two hundred twenty nine rupees, the stock was priced like a rocket. But the business runs like a train. Safe, steady, and slow.
Save this, and send it to your friend who holds I R F C. Education only, not investment advice. Follow money in cloud.
